chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
Making a bequest is a right and an established matter, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله indeed made a will; therefore, it is appropriate for the Muslim to make a bequest.

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: A bequest or will made before death regarding one's estate or obligations.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: A true, established, and rightful matter.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: The Messenger of Allah, whose practice serves as the model and proof.
key_terms.لِلْمُسْلِمِ أَنْ يُوصِيَ: That the Muslim should make a bequest.

ai.seo_question: Is making a will recommended or obligatory for a Muslim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that making a bequest is a rightful and established practice. It grounds this in the precedent of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, indicating that a Muslim should not neglect leaving a will.
